LESSON: LANGUAGE USE 5.3.1 PRESENT SIMPLE TENSE

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.3: Language Use 5.3.1 Present Simple Tense
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Language Use 5.3.1 Present Simple Tense, part of Strand 5 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How do you spend your morning to evening?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify words in the present simple tense in given sentences,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Language Use 5.3.1 Present Simple Tense in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use present tense forms to talk about routine or daily activities,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Language Use 5.3.1 Present Simple Tense in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the use of present simple tense to talk about routine activities. • Learners with low vision to watch while learners with blindness to listen to an audio-visual clip on children participating in routine activities and talk about the activities using present simple tense. • Learners are guided to individually respond to questions based on daily routines. • Learners to report what he or she does at home. • Learners are guided to individually respond to simple questions demonstrating the use of present simple tense in talking about routine activities. • Learners to repeat sentences containing present simple tense from a story, poem or conversation they have listened to. How do you spend your morning to evening?

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Language Use 5.3.1 Present Simple Tense in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.

C. appreciate the use of present simple tense to talk about routine activities. • Learners with low vision to watch while learners with blindness to listen to an audio-visual clip on children participating in routine activities and talk about the activities using present simple tense. • Learners are guided to individually respond to questions based on daily routines. • Learners to report what he or she does at home. • Learners are guided to individually respond to simple questions demonstrating the use of present simple tense in talking about routine activities. • Learners to repeat sentences containing present simple tense from a story, poem or conversation they have listened to. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Language Use 5.3.1 Present Simple Tense together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Digital literacy- The learner’s ability to interact with digital devices with assistive technology is enhanced as they watch and listen to a video on

children participating in routine activities and talk about the activities using present simple tense.

Values:
Respect is developed as the learner appreciates and understands others as they talk about their routine activities.

50

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (self-esteem)- learners acquire an enhanced level of self-esteem as they apply present tense forms to talk about time and sequence of

routine or daily activities.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Learners discuss activities taking place at different times of the day in Environmental Activities.

Suggested learning resources

• Braille letter cards

• Audio, video clip

• Textbooks in braille and in appropriate font and colour contrast.

Main points to remember:

1. identify words in the present simple tense in given sentences,
2. use present tense forms to talk about routine or daily activities,
3. appreciate the use of present simple tense to talk about routine activities. • Learners with low vision to watch while learners with blindness to listen to an audio-visual clip on children participating in routine activities and talk about the activities using present simple tense. • Learners are guided to individually respond to questions based on daily routines. • Learners to report what he or she does at home. • Learners are guided to individually respond to simple questions demonstrating the use of present simple tense in talking about routine activities. • Learners to repeat sentences containing present simple tense from a story, poem or conversation they have listened to.
